children: 0642 GMT - Tech stocks were back under pressure last week, and financial markets are wondering if this is the beginning of a greater crash, says Thomas Mathews, head of markets in Asia for Capital Economics. His base case remains that it isn't. Volatility in tech stocks should pick up as the AI bubble continues to inflate. Sharp and short-lived sell-offs were common as the dotcom bubble inflated, he adds. Still, that bubble did eventually burst, and this one will too, he says. But for now, the indicators of a bubble don't seem quite stretched enough to call time on the rally. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0641 GMT - Fears about the AI buildout are "way overblown," says Dan Ives, partner and analyst at Yorkville Ives, in a note. "We are in a market environment in which any negative data point or hint of nervousness causes panic for the tech sector as this multi-trillion AI foundation buildout is tied to a handful of major tech players," says Ives. Higher rates don't change underlying demand for the buildout, even though it does matter for debt and how the investment gets financed, Ives adds. U.S. stock futures show signs of recovering sentiment in Asian trade. Futures tied to the Nasdaq, Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 climb 1.4%, 0.4% and 0.7%, respectively. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com)
